task: What is the purpose of a tokenizer in a language model pipeline? Reply in two sentences.
expectation: Explains that a tokenizer converts text into numerical tokens (or subword units) that the model can process, and converts model output back to text.

task: What does setting temperature=0 do when generating text with an LLM? Reply in one sentence.
expectation: States that temperature=0 makes the model deterministic (or greedy), always selecting the highest-probability token.

task: If a text embedding model outputs 768-dimensional vectors, how many floating-point numbers represent a single sentence? Give just the number.
A model has a 128k token context window. If a document is 200k tokens, can it fit in a single prompt? Answer yes or no and explain in one sentence.
expectation: Says no, and explains the document exceeds the context window limit.

task: An API charges $0.50 per million input tokens and $1.50 per million output tokens. You send 500 requests, each with 2000 input tokens and 800 output tokens. What is the total cost in US dollars?
expectation: Calculates total input tokens = 1,000,000 at $0.50 = $0.50, total output tokens = 400,000 at $1.50 = $0.60, total = $1.10.

task: A document has 12,000 tokens. You want to chunk it for RAG with 500-token chunks and 50-token overlap. How many chunks will be produced? Show your working.
expectation: Each chunk advances by 450 tokens (500 - 50 overlap). 12000 / 450 = 26.67, so 27 chunks. Accepts 26 or 27 depending on handling of the final partial chunk.

task: Two embedding vectors are [1, 0, 1] and [0, 1, 1]. Calculate their cosine similarity. Give the exact answer as a simplified fraction or decimal rounded to 4 places.
expectation: Dot product = 1, magnitudes = sqrt(2) and sqrt(2), cosine = 1/2 = 0.5.

task: A provider allows 60 requests per minute. Your batch has 500 requests. How many minutes will it take to process all requests if you send exactly at the rate limit? Round up to the nearest whole minute.

A prompt has 4000 input tokens. Without caching, input costs $2.00 per million tokens. With prompt caching, the first call pays full price but subsequent calls pay 10% of the input price for cached tokens. If you make 20 identical calls, what is the total input cost with and without caching, and what percentage did caching save?

A budget controller projects worst-case cost before each call. Input price is $1.00/Mtok, output price is $5.00/Mtok. The prompt is estimated at 3000 input tokens and max_tokens is set to 2048. Remaining budget is $0.015. Should the controller admit or refuse this call? Show the projection calculation.
expectation: Projected cost = (3000 * $1.00/1M) + (2048 * $5.00/1M) = $0.003 + $0.01024 = $0.01324. Since $0.01324 <= $0.015, the controller should admit the call.

task: A model ladder has an economy rung at $0.001 per call and a frontier rung at $0.008 per call. The economy rung resolves 80% of tasks on first attempt and retries twice on failure. Using the break-even formula r* = k / (C/c - 1 + k) where k=2 retry attempts and C/c is the price ratio, what is the break-even resolution rate? Is the economy rung above or below it at 80%?
expectation: C/c = 0.008/0.001 = 8. r* = 2 / (8 - 1 + 2) = 2/9 = 0.2222 or 22.2%. Since 80% > 22.2%, the economy rung is well above break-even and is the better choice.

task: An agent run has these spans: run (100ms total), planner (20ms), tool_call (30ms), answer_node (40ms), provider_call inside answer_node (35ms). Draw the hierarchy as an indented list and identify which span accounts for the most time.
expectation: Shows run as parent, with planner, tool_call, and answer_node as children, and provider_call nested inside answer_node. Identifies answer_node (or provider_call within it) as the longest span.

task: An adversarial loop sends 100 requests against a $0.05 budget ceiling. Each admitted call costs approximately $0.001. The controller has max_calls_per_run=40. How many calls will be admitted, what will the approximate total spend be, and what stops the loop? Explain which limit triggers first.
expectation: At $0.001 per call, $0.05 budget allows ~50 calls, but max_calls_per_run=40 triggers first. So 40 calls admitted, ~$0.04 spent, stopped by the call ceiling not the dollar ceiling.

task: Model A costs $0.002 per call and resolves 95% of tasks. Model B costs $0.0005 per call and resolves 70% of tasks, with up to 3 retries on failure. Calculate cost per resolved task for each model. Which is more economical?
expectation: Model A: $0.002 / 0.95 = $0.002105 per resolved task. Model B: average calls per resolved task considering retries needs calculation. With 70% success rate and 3 attempts: expected calls = 1*0.7 + 2*0.3*0.7 + 3*0.3*0.3*0.7 + 3*0.3^3 = about 1.58 calls per task, but only resolves at rate 1-0.3^3 = 97.3%. Cost per resolved = (1.58 * $0.0005) / 0.973 = ~$0.000812. Model B is more economical per resolved task.

task: A metrics system creates one time series per unique label combination. You have labels: provider (3 values), model (5 values), status (3 values). How many time series does this create? Now explain why adding user_id (100,000 users) as a label would be problematic.
expectation: 3 * 5 * 3 = 45 time series. Adding user_id: 45 * 100,000 = 4,500,000 time series. This high cardinality would overwhelm the metrics backend with memory and storage requirements.

task: A model with hidden reasoning uses max_tokens=512. It spends 480 tokens on reasoning and 32 tokens on the visible answer. The provider charges $0.75 per million output tokens. What is the cost of the visible answer alone vs the total billed cost? What percentage of the bill produced useful output?
expectation: Total billed: 512 * $0.75/1M = $0.000384. Visible answer cost: 32 * $0.75/1M = $0.000024. Percentage useful: 32/512 = 6.25% of the bill produced visible output.
